summary: Round 1 spec review found four Blocker findings in plan.md: the audit check has no named file or invocation, no target versions or major-upgrade rule are named, no phase names the files it changes, and no record destination is named. Review is complete; the role gate also fails on a baseline scope mismatch that the orchestrator must correct.
blocking_findings: F1 [Blocker] plan.md Task 1.1: The red audit check has no named file, command, or exit-code contract, and Task 1.3 names no bundle equality command. Rationale: The task says only 'a script or test' and 'the bundle equality check'; the standard treats an unnamed file location and CLI shape as a design choice left to the implementer.

F2 [Blocker] plan.md Tasks 1.2 and 2.1: No target versions and no rule for a major upgrade that breaks tests. Rationale: bun outdated shows major steps for vitest 2 to 5, happy-dom 15 to 21, solid-js 1 to 2, TypeScript 5 to 7, @opencode/plugin 2.0.32 to 2.3.2 and @opentui 0.6.6 to 0.9.7; bun audit --json shows happy-dom high ranges <=20.8.7 and <=20.14.6 and a high launch-editor advisory at vite <=6.4.2, so the plan must name which versions clear the highs and what happens when a major step breaks bun test or vitest.

F3 [Blocker] plan.md Tasks 1.2 and 2.1: Neither phase names the files to create or change. Rationale: FR-1 and FR-2 name two package.json and two bun.lock files, FR-5 names panel/main.ts and panel/main.js, and the guard breaking-change fixes affect source files, but the tasks say only 'package updates and code fixes'; the standard requires each phase to name its files.

F4 [Blocker] plan.md Tasks 1.3 and 2.2: The record destinations are unnamed. Rationale: FR-2, FR-3 and the acceptance criteria require a written reason per remaining advisory and a moderate/low list, but the tasks say only 'records'; the implementer must choose the file location and the record of PM acceptance.
nonblocking_findings: F5 [Major] plan.md Phase 1 and Phase 2: No normal or edge test cases are named. Rationale: The plan lists verification commands but no cases such as one critical in either folder fails, zero critical and high passes, and moderate-only stays passing; the standard requires named normal and edge cases per phase.

F6 [Nit] spec.md Overview: The PM dates 2026-11-23 and 2026-11-25 appear in the spec but are not attached to plan tasks. Rationale: The phase order implies the dates, so the omission does not change what the implementer builds, but the plan should state the deadline on each task.
